sections.text: When thy reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then shalt thou become indifferent both to the philosophies thou hast heard and to those thou mayest yet hear.
When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scripts, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the Infinite, then hast thou attained Spirituality.

Arjuna asked: My Lord! How can we recognise the saint who has attained Pure Intellect, who has reached this state of Bliss, and whose mind is steady? how does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?

We had been discussing chapter two. We had been discussing verse 47 onwards, the most quoted verse in Bhagavad Gita, which is Karmani Vadikarastha. Between that verse 47 and verse 53, Bhagavan gives us concisely and succinctly how to live life. These scriptures give advice about how to live your life -- sometimes Hinduism is called a way of life. So from verse 47 onward, what we have seen is the reality of my life.
Reality of my life is: I am a living being, a conscious being, and therefore activity is what makes me who I am. I must be active. However, I must understand that the only thing which is in my control is my actions. The result of my actions are not in my control simply because there is infinite world out there that is the field of my actions. When I act in this field of my actions, the other forces affect the result of my actions which is not in my control. So I must keep the goal very high, which gives me the directions of my actions. So the goal gives us direction.
Bhagavad Gita did not say dont have any goal. It says Karmaniyeva adhikara ste ma faleshukadachan, not the fruits of action. It did not say dont keep any goal or dont plan anything in your life, just continue so keep the goal in your mind and then work accordingly. So the goal gives me direction in which direction I should put my actions. If Im going from here to New York, I know one thing, I have to drive northward on 95, that my goal is to go to New York. It gives me direction which way to go, so I dont drive south.
What it does not give me is what I will encounter on my way while Im driving. I can generally predict that because Im driving at 70 miles an hour and New York is 400 miles from here, it should take me about six hours. But the goal does not give me all the other information which might affect my reaching New York. Previously we didnt have any way to predict whats going to happen on the way, so we had to rely only on our general judgment. And there was some traffic news broadcast which would tell us what the traffic pattern was that day.
Then we have now the gps. Were trying to add more and more ability to predict what is going to affect my travel. My GPS also tells me there is traffic congestion 25 miles from here and it will last for 8 miles. May delay for 15 minutes. So would you like to take a detour? Every time I try to follow my GPS agna to take detour, Im actually more delayed than the 15 minutes that GPS predicted.
Because GPS does have some information but not all information. It had information on my main route but didnt really have all the information about the detour I would have to take. So I figured out that I better stay on the same course which I have started and decided upon. The point is that Karma Phala is dependent on not just one factor but many factors which we may not have control over. Therefore you should not be worried about the Karma Phala because it is not in your hand. Karma is your right, thats what is in your control.
Find a direction, find a goal in life. Find a direction and work accordingly. Karma Phala may not be because whats going to encounter while youre working, you will not know. And therefore he said ma karma fala hatu bahu. Therefore do not make the fruits as the motivator. Well reach New York in six hours.
Because Im driving at 70 miles an hour, that should not be the motivating force of my driving. My motivation is I need to reach New York and it is in north. Therefore Im driving northward. I will deal with whatever comes in my way. If I have to take a detour, Ill take a detour. But I will reach New York.
I dont know, but I will reach there. But never get discouraged and say, oh, there is a lot of traffic today. Ma sanghatu akarmani. Do not get attached to inaction because you predict there may be a lot of obstructions on your way. So this is the prescription given to us. Have a goal, find a direction and then continue working.
Do not worry about what you will encounter. So the next verse says Siddhi asiddhi samo bhatva Yogastha kurukarman. Establish yourself in yoga and then work. Now when I say yoga, I dont mean yoga classes -- Panditji keeps telling me to go, but I keep avoiding. So now I cant do anything about that.
Yogastha kurukarman means establish yourself into a state of mind where success and failure do not affect you. Say I have to go to New York but right near Ashland theres a huge traffic jam. That doesnt make me make a U-turn and come back home. My goal is to get there, to somehow find a way to get over this obstacle. Therefore he said siddhi asiddhi samo bhatva -- whatever comes in your way, take it equally.
This is still part of your life. So the yoga is samatvam Yoga uchate. I should be establishing myself in yoga. Its very simple: keep your mind even in whatever situation you encounter. In other words, keep that goal still in your mind. Dont let that obstruction in your way discourage you. Your goal is to achieve that infinite happiness. Dont get discouraged. Success and failure are part of your life because it is guaranteed that sometimes you will succeed, and most of the time you will fail. We used to track the statistics -- what is our hit rate on our proposals? For a while I did that because I was trained by my previous employers to track the hit rate.
Then I said boy these hit rates look very poor. Lets not look at it, lets stop this thing. Just keep doing what you are doing because if you get discouraged by the results then you will stop acting. Goal is to achieve what you want to achieve. So Bhagawan said samatam yoga uchathe keep your mind equanimous in all situation with the success or failures. Thats very necessary because failures are going to be there.
And then when you work in that manner you will be applying your full focus and therefore you will be very efficient in your actions. So we saw the next definition of yogas Yogaha Karma Sukhaoshalam. When do I consider myself to be established in the samatvam? My actions become efficient. We all know this. When Im fully focusing on what Im doing, Im efficient. But sometimes I take work home and then I also want to watch the shows which I missed last time -- they are on DVR now, all recorded.
Im trying to do my work and trying to pay attention to the show. Whats going on? See, the work was supposed to take me two hours; it takes me about eight hours. And then I say, The whole weekend I was working. Anil, you were truly not working eight hours. So I am not efficient in my actions.
When my actions are efficient, I should consider myself to be established in yoga. That was the prescription in the beginning. Bhagavan said Yogasthakura Karmani, establish yourself in yoga, have your mind steady and focused and work in this world. Thats the way of life. Thats why I say Hinduism teaches you what is the way of life. And succinctly told you how to be successful and happy in life.
The next few verses say, the one who now established in this yoga, he gives up all this Sukruta duskrita Buddhi yukto jahaati ha ubhe sukruta duskrita. Once you are completely focused in doing your best, you will not be affected by the results or whether it is a good or bad. You know you have done your best. You couldnt have done any better than this. The law of karma says the actions which you have put forth will bear results sooner or later. It does happen that sometimes I go to a client and make a presentation, and he doesnt give me the work.
But then he tells somebody else two years later, Why dont you talk to such and such? I thought he was pretty good. He didnt give me the job, but he refers me to somebody. And that third person comes and gives me a job. Because I put my efforts into the presentation to the first client, it eventually bore fruit -- but I dont make that connection.
Therefore my mind cannot see why Im getting this work but not that one. Thats the law of karma. What I call it Prarabdha is not something completely random which is happening to my life but something happening in present. I cannot make a connection to my past actions. I call it my Prarabdha. So therefore Bhagavan says, one who acts in this world with that even mindedness he will be beyond sukruta duskrita.
He will be beyond good and bad. Many people used to say or still say doing good is good enough. Why do I have to worry about all these things? And Karma Yoga and this yoga just do good in life. Actually I remember Subhas Pahuja. He came to this class few times before he passed away.
And his standard thing why do you have to learn Bhagavad Gita? I know doing good is good and I said that Bhagavan says doing good is not good enough. Why that good is Binding you, the expectation of good results and that becomes your golden chain. Every time I do good, I expect at least somebody will recognize. And our granddaughter, when she does something, she is looking around to see whether everybody is paying attention. Then if nobody pays attention, she herself says, Medha is so smart.
Thats our true nature. We want recognition right from the childhood. We want to see around whether anybodys paying attention. Because Im doing good but nobodys paying attention. What is good about that? So that good is binding me to good results in good vasanas but still vasanas.
Therefore Bhagawan said, you will be relieved from both the good and bad if you focus on your actions only and not the results. Results are guaranteed. Something which is guaranteed, you dont have to worry about it. We know the sun will rise tomorrow. We dont have to agonize last night about what will happen tomorrow morning -- will the sun rise? We know it is guaranteed.
Results of actions are guaranteed. And therefore you shouldnt be worried about that. Karmajam, budhiyuktahi, falam taktva, manishinah, janma, bandha, vinur muktaha, padam gachanti, anamayam. We are afraid of all the evils in this world which creates sorrows in our life. And Bhagavan said, the one who is established in this yoga and working in this world he will go beyond anamayam. He will go beyond all evils.
Karma jam buddhiktahi falam kyakvam. Those wise one possessed of this knowledge who has given up the karma phala, given up in a sense given up the anxiety about karma phala. Whatever is in my way. They get janma, bandha, vinir muktaha. They get relieved from the cycles on birth and death. Its obviously very, very Hindu concept of the punar janma.
But even in this life, I take this position and then I take that position. Every position I take in this life is because of what? Because of my vasanas. I want to be a president of this, and I want to be the chairperson of that. I want to be on this board, I want to do this -- it is all driven by my vasanas, my egocentric desires.

Verse 52 describes a sign of progress: When thy reason has crossed the entanglements of illusion, then shalt thou become indifferent both to the philosophies thou hast heard and to those thou mayest yet hear. At a certain stage, the seeker no longer needs to accumulate more information - they have moved from learning about truth to experiencing it directly. The teachings that once seemed so important become stepping stones now left behind.
Verse 53 describes the goal: When the intellect, bewildered by the multiplicity of holy scripts, stands unperturbed in blissful contemplation of the Infinite, then hast thou attained Spirituality. The mind that was once confused by competing philosophies and practices becomes still and one-pointed. Then in verse 54, Arjuna asks the practical question that opens the final section of the chapter: How can we recognise the saint who has attained Pure Intellect... how does he talk, how does he live, and how does he act?
This question is crucial for us too. Having heard the theory, we want to know what it looks like in practice. Reflect today: Do you know anyone who embodies this teaching - someone who seems consistently peaceful regardless of circumstances, who acts with skill and dedication yet without visible anxiety about results? What qualities do you observe in them? Also ask: What would it look like if you had crossed the entanglements of illusion? How would your daily life be different? Let this vision inspire your practice.
